explanations.16: The ?? operator means 'use the right side if the left side is null or undefined', so this safely defaults to 0 if counts.helpful doesn't exist.
explanations.19: This calculates what percentage of votes were helpful, rounding to a whole number; if there are zero total votes, it returns 0 to avoid dividing by zero.
explanations.24: This sorts the array first by helpful count (highest first), then by total votes as a tiebreaker — the || means 'if the first comparison is tied, use the second'.
explanations.27: Same percentage calculation as line 19, but for the overall approval rate across all articles combined.
explanations.68: The style object sets the width of the progress bar fill to match the approval ratio as a CSS percentage string.
explanations.100: The backticks create a template literal, which is a fancy string that lets you insert variables (siteUrl and slug) directly using ${} syntax.
explanations.102: rel="noopener noreferrer" is a security setting that prevents the opened page from accessing the original window object, protecting users on untrusted sites.
explanations.143: e.preventDefault() stops the browser from doing its default form submission (which would reload the page), letting us handle it with custom code instead.
explanations.167: This is a constant string used as the key name when storing and retrieving the admin token from the browser's localStorage.
explanations.185: window.location.hash gives you everything after the # in the URL; .slice(1) removes that # character, so you're left with just the token if one exists.
explanations.190: useCallback wraps a function so that it only gets recreated if one of its dependencies changes, preventing unnecessary re-renders of child components.
explanations.196: encodeURIComponent() safely escapes special characters in the token so they don't break the URL when passed as a query parameter.
explanations.197: A 403 status code means 'Forbidden' — the server rejected the request because the token is invalid.
explanations.213: [apiUrl] tells React to recreate fetchData only when apiUrl changes, keeping the function stable between renders unless the URL actually changes.
explanations.219: This effect runs whenever token changes and calls fetchData — it's how the dashboard automatically refreshes data when you log in or restore a saved token.
explanations.234: If data exists, computeTotals processes it into summary stats; otherwise stats is null (which prevents rendering the dashboard until data is loaded).
